text:
B: Hiya, you alright? I'm Daniel.
A: Alright. Callum.
B: Nice one. Where are you calling from, Callum?
A: Swindon.
B: Swindon, okay. I'm Peterborough. Not too far off, sort of. Is that your PS5 in the background there?
A: Yeah. Controller's drifting though, need a new one.
B: Ah, nightmare. What you playing, FIFA?
A: EA FC mostly, yeah. And a bit of Call of Duty. Late, usually.
B: I used to be decent at FIFA at uni, now I just get destroyed by twelve-year-olds online. So what do you do, are you working or...?
A: Not at the minute. I was assistant manager at a sports shop, on the retail park, and they restructured the branch about four months ago, so I took redundancy. Been applying for stuff since. So, yeah.
B: Ah, sorry, mate. That's rubbish. How long were you there?
A: Erm, a good few years. I've done retail since I was eighteen, sales assistant, then supervisor, then assistant manager. I knew the stock inside out, trainers and that. Deliveries, cashing up. The shop floor side I was fine with. It was the paperwork and the rotas I wasn't great at, to be honest.
B: Ha, yeah, rotas. That's my whole life. I'm in a distribution centre, I manage the operations side, so it's shift patterns, staffing, lorries turning up late. I've got colour-coded spreadsheets, my wife thinks I need help.
A: That's sort of what I'm looking at, actually. Warehouse. There's a load of distribution centres off the M4. Something with a regular rota, no weekend lates.
B: Yeah, there's always stuff going round Swindon. And honestly, someone who's run a shop floor and can deal with awkward customers, that's half of what a shift supervisor does. Handling people who are having a bad day. You'd be surprised how many people can't do that.
A: Yeah?
B: Yeah. The system stuff you learn in a few weeks. What you can't teach is someone who turns up and doesn't flap. What were your customers like?
A: Erm, mixed. You'd get dads kicking off about the price of school football boots in August. I just let them get it out and then sort it. Didn't bother me really.
B: That's exactly it. Get them to vent, then sort it. Do you follow football as well, or just play the games?
A: Bit of both. Swindon Town, but they're rubbish again this season. I mostly just check the score on my phone.
B: Ha, I hear you. I'm Posh, Peterborough United. Season ticket on and off, I go with my dad. It's character-building, let's put it that way.
A: Yeah. I used to go the County Ground a lot with my dad, not so much now.
B: Do you play at all? Five-a-side?
A: Used to. The lad who organised it moved away, so it sort of fizzled out.
B: That always happens, it's always one bloke holding the whole thing together. I play Wednesdays with some lads from work. Honestly if you get a warehouse job, ask about five-a-side, there's always a team.
A: Yeah, maybe. That'd be alright actually.
B: Out of interest, have you got your CV pitched at warehouse stuff, or is it still all retail wording?
A: Erm, I dunno. Probably still retail, I haven't really changed it.
B: Might be worth a tweak, mate. Put the deliveries and the stock bit right at the top, because that's what they'll—
